name: Custom Reusable Stickers
seoTitle: Custom Reusable Stickers: Removable and Restickable Vinyl
seoDescription: Custom reusable stickers you can peel off and put back: static cling, removable vinyl and low-tack options for glass, walls, laptops and events. Free proof.
tagline: Peel it off, stick it back on: static cling and removable vinyl built for repeated use.
quickAnswer: Custom reusable stickers are printed stickers that peel off and reapply without tearing or leaving residue. We make them three ways: static cling film with no adhesive for glass, removable adhesive vinyl for walls and laptops, and low-tack repositionable vinyl for planners and displays. They suit events, seasonal promotions, rentals and kids. From $0.30 per sticker, 100 minimum, 5 to 7 business days production.
highlights: Material: static cling or removable vinyl

sections.h2: Stickers that come back off, and go back on, without a fight
sections.html:
Can you reuse vinyl stickers? Only if they were made to be reused. A standard sticker is built to stay: permanent adhesive, a liner you throw away, and once it is on, it is on. A reusable sticker swaps that for a hold you can break and remake many times, which changes the material, the adhesive and how it is packed. The nearest sibling is our custom window sticker range, which includes static cling for glass; the difference is that window stickers are built around glass specifically, while this page covers reusable constructions for any smooth surface, from a laptop lid and a painted wall to a whiteboard, a locker or a car door for a weekend event.

We print them for pop-up shops, sports teams swapping sponsor marks, schools, trade show booths, rental fleets, planners and sticker books, and parents who would rather the dinosaur moved rooms than stayed on the fridge forever.

sections.h2: Three ways to make a sticker reusable
sections.html:
There is no single reusable material. Pick the construction by surface and by how many times it will move.

ConstructionHow it holdsSurfacesRe-usesBest for
Static clingSoft vinyl grips by surface contact, no adhesiveGlass, mirrors, glossy acrylic onlyDozens, if kept cleanWindow promotions, parking permits, seasonal decor
Removable adhesive vinylLow-residue adhesive that releases cleanlyPainted walls, laptops, metal, plastic, glass5 to 10 before the tack weakensWall graphics, event branding, laptop and locker stickers
Repositionable low-tack vinylVery light adhesive, slides into place then holdsPaper, whiteboards, displays, plannersMany, on clean surfacesPlanner stickers, schedule boards, sticker books

Static cling is the most reusable but the fussiest about surfaces: it will not hold on a wall or a laptop. Removable adhesive goes almost anywhere but has a limited number of lifts. If the sticker lives on glass, choose cling; everywhere else, choose removable.

sections.h2: Surfaces where a reusable sticker holds, and where it will not
sections.html:
• Glass, mirrors and glossy acrylic: static cling and removable vinyl both work. Clean with soap and water, not glass cleaner, before the first application.
  • Painted drywall: removable vinyl only, on paint cured at least a month. Flat and matte paints hold better than fresh satin; textured walls lower the grip.
  • Laptops, phone cases, metal lockers: removable vinyl, matte laminate recommended so the print survives being handled on every move.
  • Whiteboards and planners: repositionable low-tack vinyl; it will not pull ink off the board or tear the page.
  • Car doors for an event weekend: removable vinyl on a clean, cured paint, applied dry, removed within a few weeks. Not for months in the sun.
  • Brick, fabric, unsealed wood, silicone: none of the three will hold. Use a magnet or a sign instead.

sections.h2: How to store reusable stickers between uses
sections.html:
Most reusable stickers die in a drawer, not on the wall. Dust and lint on the back are what stop a cling or a removable sticker from holding the second time.

  1. Peel slowly from one corner at a low angle. Pulling straight out stretches the vinyl and leaves a wrinkle that never flattens.
  2. Put it straight back on its original liner, or on the backing sheet we include with every reusable order. Smooth it down so no air is trapped.
  3. If the liner is lost, stick it to a clean sheet of glossy card or a page protector. Never plain paper; it bonds and tears.
  4. Store flat, out of sunlight, between 50°F and 80°F. A folder or envelope is better than a loose pile.
  5. Before reusing, rinse a static cling in lukewarm water and let it air dry face down. For removable vinyl, wipe the back lightly with a damp cloth and let it dry fully.
  6. Apply to a clean surface. The sticker cannot hold on dust, grease or fresh paint however clean its back is.

sections.h2: What the print has to survive when a sticker moves around
sections.html: A sticker that gets handled every month needs a tougher print than one that stays put. We laminate removable vinyl by default, in gloss or matte, so fingernails and the edge of a liner do not scratch the color. Static cling is printed on the front and left unlaminated so it stays soft enough to grip glass, which is why it belongs indoors or on the inside of a window, not outside. Keep designs free of thin spikes and fine lettering under 6 pt; a point tears on the third peel. Sizes run from 0.5" to 24" x 36", though anything over 12" is easier to reposition with two people. For a sticker that has to be visible in a dark room as well, our glow in the dark sticker range can be made with the same removable adhesive.

Tell us where the sticker will go and how many times it will move, and we will pick the construction, or say outright which row of the table you want. Send artwork as a vector file (AI, EPS, SVG, PDF) or a 300 dpi PNG or JPG at final size; free design support can tidy a logo or build a sticker from scratch. Choose gloss or matte and the shape, which can be die cut to the artwork or a standard circle, square or rectangle. The minimum is 100 stickers per design, prices start at $0.30 and depend on size, quantity and construction, and production is 5 to 7 business days after you approve the free proof. Shipping by FedEx in the United States is free. Every reusable order ships with spare backing sheets. Our other materials and finishes are listed on the Die Cut Stickers home page.

faqs.q: Can you reuse vinyl stickers that were printed with normal adhesive?
faqs.a: Usually not. A permanent adhesive sticker stretches and loses most of its tack on the first peel, and the adhesive stays on the surface. Reusable stickers are made with static cling, removable or low-tack constructions from the start, which is why they come off clean and go back on.

faqs.q: How many times can a custom reusable sticker be reapplied?
faqs.a: Static cling on clean glass can be moved dozens of times. Removable adhesive vinyl manages 5 to 10 lifts before the tack weakens, and low-tack repositionable vinyl keeps going as long as the back stays free of dust. Storing each one on its liner between uses is what preserves the count.

faqs.q: What is the best way to store reusable stickers so they keep sticking?
faqs.a: Put them back on their original liner or the backing sheet we ship with the order, smooth out trapped air and store them flat in a folder away from sunlight. Dust on the adhesive side is the usual reason a sticker stops holding, so keep the back covered whenever it is off the wall.

faqs.q: Will restickable stickers hold on a painted wall?
faqs.a: Removable adhesive vinyl will, on paint that has cured for at least a month. Flat and matte paints hold best; textured or freshly painted walls lower the grip. Static cling will not hold on a wall at all, since it relies on a glossy surface like glass or acrylic.

faqs.q: Do removable stickers leave residue on a laptop or locker?
faqs.a: No, if peeled slowly from a corner at a low angle. The adhesive is formulated to release from the surface rather than split. Leaving the sticker on for years in direct heat can change that, so for a laptop that lives in a hot car, plan on moving it before the sticker bakes on.

faqs.q: Can static cling stickers go on the outside of a window?
faqs.a: They are happier inside. Static cling has no adhesive, so wind, rain and heat on an exterior pane will lift it within days. Apply it to the inside of the glass facing out, or choose removable adhesive vinyl if the sticker must sit on the outside surface.

faqs.q: Can reusable stickers be die cut to the shape of my logo?
faqs.a: Yes. Both static cling and removable vinyl can be cut to the artwork outline. Avoid thin spikes, narrow letters and points under 0.125" wide, because those tear on the second or third peel. A slightly rounded outline or a thin border keeps a reusable sticker intact for years of moves.

faqs.q: Are reusable stickers suitable for a kid's bedroom wall?
faqs.a: Yes. Removable vinyl is the usual choice: it holds on cured paint, moves when the room is rearranged and comes off clean when the child outgrows it. Keep the designs 2" or larger so small hands can peel them without tearing, and store spares on the backing sheet.

faqs.q: Which reusable sticker works on a whiteboard or planner?
faqs.a: Low-tack repositionable vinyl. It slides into place, holds on the board or page, and lifts without pulling marker ink or tearing paper. Standard removable vinyl is too grippy for planner pages, and static cling will not hold on the matte surface of a whiteboard.

faqs.q: How many custom reusable stickers do I have to order?
faqs.a: The minimum is 100 stickers per design. Prices start at $0.30 per sticker and depend on the size, the quantity and which of the three constructions you choose. A set of designs for one event or one product can share an order, with the quantity split between them.

faqs.q: Can I use removable stickers on a car for a weekend event?
faqs.a: Yes, on clean, cured factory paint, applied dry and removed within a few weeks. Peel while the panel is warm but not hot, from a corner, at a low angle. Do not leave event stickers on through a summer; months of sun turn a removable adhesive into a permanent one.

faqs.q: Are custom removable stickers printed to the same quality as permanent ones?
faqs.a: Yes. They go through the same full-color CMYK press with Pantone matching, and removable vinyl gets the same gloss or matte laminate as our permanent stickers. The only unlaminated option is static cling, which stays bare so the film remains soft enough to grip glass.
